title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts
claim: One model supports both classic click-based segmentation and a new capability: segmenting all instances of a concept from text or exemplars.
layout: 2 panels split by divider; image rows over video rows; prompt legend underneath
description: A wide figure split by a vertical divider into two columns. The left column, titled Promptable Visual Segmentation, has an Image row showing a humpback whale masked in yellow with a green positive and a pink negative click, and a Video row of three cat frames masked in teal with click markers. The right column, titled Promptable Concept Segmentation, shows an image row with three photos (striped cats, round cells, small window), each with a text label tab and colored instance masks. Green solid boxes and pink dashed boxes mark positive and negative exemplars. Below that, two video strips show kangaroos and workers in hard hats, with colored masks per instance. Legends at the bottom explain click prompts and noun-phrase or exemplar prompts. The eye goes first to the colorful masks on the photos.
caption: SAM 3 improves over SAM 2 on promptable visual segmentation with clicks (left) and introduces the new promptable concept segmentation capability (right). Users can segment all instances of a visual concept specified by a short noun phrase, image exemplars (positive or negative), or a combination of both.
abstract: We present Segment Anything Model (SAM) 3, a unified model that detects, segments, and tracks objects in images and videos based on concept prompts, which we define as either short noun phrases (e.g., "yellow school bus"), image exemplars, or a combination of both. Promptable Concept Segmentation (PCS) takes such prompts and returns segmentation masks and unique identities for all matching object instances. To advance PCS, we build a scalable data engine that produces a high-quality dataset with 4M unique concept labels, including hard negatives, across images and videos. Our model consists of an image-level detector and a memory-based video tracker that share a single backbone. Recognition and localization are decoupled with a presence head, which boosts detection accuracy. SAM 3 doubles the accuracy of existing systems in both image and video PCS, and improves previous SAM capabilities on visual segmentation tasks. We open source SAM 3 along with our new Segment Anything with Concepts (SA-Co) benchmark for promptable concept segmentation.
